title: Mask Atelier
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk, mask craftsman Lu Qing（A mask craftsman around forty, indigo short jacket dusted with pigment powder, right hand often gripping a wolf-hair brush, brows deeply furrowed） pushes open the papier-mache atelier（A street-front papier-mache atelier; half-dry mask shells dry on wooden racks, unpainted white blanks hang on the wall） wooden door, both hands cradling the freshly papier-mached white-faced Cao Cao headdress（A freshly papier-mached white-faced Cao Cao headdress, silk beard black and neat, gold leaf on the crest still unworn）.

A row of five tung-oil lamps（A row of five tung-oil iron lamps hanging under the papier-mache atelier beam, shades yellowed by soot） hangs under the papier-mache atelier beam; Lu Qing wipes soot from each with a cloth.

Two pairs of copper clappers（Two pairs of copper clappers hanging by the door, faces carved with key patterns, lightly knocking when wind passes） hang by the door; Lu Qing brushes them and they ring clear and bright.
Lu Qing sets the white-faced Cao Cao headdress on a wooden stand and combs the silk beard smooth with a bamboo comb.
Lu Qing rests against the mask-shell drying rack; tung-oil lamplight falls on his indigo short jacket.

Lu Qing opens the thread-bound face-pattern model book（A thread-bound face-pattern model book, vermilion and ink sketching painted-face formulas on xuan paper, cover stamped with a 'Lu's' vermilion seal） and checks it against the headdress formula.
He uses a vermilion brush to fill in painted-face brow lines and eye-socket finishes in the blank margins.
Lu Qing closes the model book and moves the white-faced Cao Cao headdress under a dust cover.

In the morning stage side chamber（An old opera house side chamber; half a red carpet runs to the stage lip, greasepaint dishes piled by the makeup mirror）, Lu Qing greets young A-Tang（A fifteen-year-old apprentice girl with twin topknots, a vermilion bib apron, vermilion paint on her fingertips, keen eyes） dragging in the vermilion lacquer prop chest（A large vermilion lacquer prop chest, twin-dragon relief on the lid, copper lock gleaming, blue cloth lining）.
A-Tang opens the vermilion lacquer prop chest and takes out still-wet greasepaint dishes.

Lu Qing points to the three cinnabar dishes（Three celadon cinnabar dishes with undried vermilion in the wells, set on the atelier windowsill） on the windowsill and teaches A-Tang to judge thick from thin.
A-Tang squats by the side-chamber red carpet and curiously touches the twin-dragon relief on the prop chest.

In the headdress storeroom（A narrow headdress storeroom; wooden racks packed with beards and velvet pompons of every color, dust drifting in light shafts）, A-Lin（A youth whose face closely resembles A-Tang's, but with a peacock-plume hairpin worn askew and an ink-blue apron, swaggering expression） with the peacock plume askew turns from behind a wooden rack.
A-Lin parts a row of beards with fingertips; the ink-blue apron picks up dust.
A-Lin carries an empty greasepaint bucket through the far end of the headdress storeroom.
In the stage side chamber, A-Tang and A-Lin brush past each other—one in a vermilion apron, one with a peacock plume askew.
A-Tang shields the white blank in her arms; A-Lin flicks the peacock plume and skirts the mirror stand.
They part before the makeup mirror and walk opposite ways.
Months later on a rainy night, Lu Qing keeps watch alone in the papier-mache atelier, the white-faced Cao Cao headdress on his knees.

Lu Qing opens the face-pattern model book（The same face-pattern model book soaked through with tung oil, cover sticky, formulas bled into a blur）; the cover is soaked through with tung oil, formulas blurred into a paste.
Lu Qing carefully wipes oil flecks from the headdress gold-leaf edge, expression grave.
The opera season stretches long; day after day Lu Qing mixes white powder, brushes base lacquer, and waits for hemp cores to dry in the shade.
Another snowy night, he tightens his indigo short jacket and trims tangled beards beside the tung-oil lamp.
At opening season, Lu Qing stands by the door tallying headdress loads carried out.
At high-summer noon he fans half-dry mask shells slowly with a fine fan.
Autumn rain falls on end; the atelier smells of tung oil, cinnabar, and damp xuan paper.
Another New Year's Eve, Lu Qing lines beards on wooden racks and keeps vigil alone in the atelier till dawn.
At dawn Lu Qing patrols along the stage side chamber; the vermilion lacquer prop chest leans by the mirror.
Lu Qing crouches to check whether the prop chest copper lock is fully bitten shut.
Lu Qing rearranges scattered greasepaint dishes by black, white, and vermilion.

An indigo-cloth prop box（An indigo-cloth-covered prop box with no twin-dragon relief, utterly unlike the vermilion prop chest） is carried into the side chamber—no twin-dragon relief, not the vermilion lacquer prop chest.
Fire breaks at midnight; thick smoke fills the papier-mache atelier, drying racks creaking in the heat.

In the glare of flame, the white face lacquer of the white-faced Cao Cao headdress（The same white-faced Cao Cao headdress: white face cracked open to hemp cloth core, beard tangled, gold leaf peeling） cracks open, exposing the hemp cloth core.
In the side chamber, fire tongues lick the lid of the vermilion lacquer prop chest; the copper lock darkens with heat.

The vermilion lacquer prop chest（The vermilion prop chest scorched by fire, lid collapsed, twin-dragon relief charred and incomplete） finally burns and collapses; the twin-dragon relief is charred and incomplete.
Lu Qing lunges for the cracked white-faced Cao Cao headdress and clutches it hard against his chest.
The day after the fire, Lu Qing stands in the papier-mache atelier, left hand lifting the cracked white-faced Cao Cao headdress.
On a blank page of the face-pattern model book Lu Qing sketches the burned-through chest lock and notes the date the vermilion lacquer prop chest burned.
Half a copper lock from the vermilion lacquer prop chest hangs by the wall; Lu Qing wraps the still-blackened bolt in cloth.
He takes down one of the five tung-oil lamps from the beam and sits alone by its faint light.
At the end of the prop inventory Lu Qing adds the costumes once packed in the vermilion lacquer prop chest; the brush tip trembles slightly.
Weeks later, Lu Qing scrapes away the cracked lacquer layer and begins rebacking the white-faced Cao Cao headdress.

He takes out a replica white-faced helmet（A half-finished replica white-faced helmet, shaped like the Cao Cao headdress but without a beard, gold leaf replaced by yellow paper） to check the shape—it looks like the true headdress but has no beard, and the gold leaf is only yellow paper.

After the new hemp core is pressed flat and powdered again, the white-faced Cao Cao headdress（The white-faced Cao Cao headdress after rebacking: white face smooth, beard re-combed, gold leaf patched but slightly paler） is usable once more, gold leaf slightly paler.
Lu Qing divides the rebacked beard into three neat locks with a bamboo comb.

A bamboo opera basket（A bamboo-woven opera basket holding water sleeves rather than headdresses—nothing like the vermilion prop chest） is carried into the stage side chamber packed with water sleeves—nothing to do with the burned vermilion lacquer prop chest.

Troupe master Old Xue（A lean troupe master also in an indigo short jacket, but with an ivory name-plaque on his chest; build close to Lu Qing's） enters the side chamber and talks beside Lu Qing; both wear indigo short jackets.
Old Xue points at the bamboo opera basket and asks for a separate water-sleeve rack; Lu Qing notes the size in the model-book margin.

From the next street comes Xiao Ju（A girl from the neighboring embroidery shop in a pale-pink apron; at a glance she resembles young A-Tang, but wears a single braid and shy eyes） in a pale-pink apron; at a glance she somewhat resembles young A-Tang.
Xiao Ju tries to tidy a beard, but Lu Qing shakes his head—she wears a single braid; she is not A-Tang after all.

Years later at dusk, Lu Qing（The same Lu Qing: right arm wrapped in white cloth burned by raw lacquer, brush switched to the left hand, jacket cuff charred black） with his right arm wrapped in white cloth stands under the empty stage of the abandoned opera house（The abandoned opera house main hall; a corner of roof tiles collapsed, half a table drape still on the empty stage）.
Those two pairs of copper clappers by the abandoned opera house door knock lightly in the wind; Lu Qing stops to listen.
Lu Qing presses his left palm to the cold stone pillar, as if saying goodbye.
By day, adult A-Tang（A woman master in her early twenties, still wearing the vermilion apron, hair in a neat bun, steady gaze） returns along the alley and hurries toward the abandoned opera house.
Under the empty stage A-Tang reunites with arms-folded Lu Qing; they embrace.
Beside the opera-house wooden couch, A-Tang holds Lu Qing's withered hand.
Lu Qing（Lu Qing has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the workshop wooden couch, indigo short jacket covering his chest）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and dies with eyes shut.
Behind the atelier door Lu Qing's old indigo short jacket still hangs; A-Tang brushes pigment powder from the cuff.
Under the lintel, adult A-Tang straightens the tilted Lu's wooden plaque（A black-lacquer wooden plaque hung on the atelier lintel, gilt letters 'Lu's Headdresses', paint chipped at the corners）.
A-Tang polishes the four gilt letters 'Lu's Headdresses' with a fine cloth.

A-Lin（A-Lin after a makeover still wears the peacock plume askew; a greasepaint scar on the temple, expression deeper） after a makeover arrives from outside the opera house and locks eyes with A-Tang under the empty stage.
A-Tang and A-Lin stand side by side in the abandoned opera house—one calm, one sombre.
The gongs and drums soften; the youth who once touched the twin-dragon relief by the side-chamber red carpet reappears.
Lamplight returns to the papier-mache atelier; a white-faced headdress is set firmly on a wooden stand for the first time.
Dust rises again in the headdress storeroom; the figure with peacock plume askew and ink-blue apron passes the wooden racks.
That row of five tung-oil iron lamps under the atelier beam lights one by one in the dark.
The side chamber with the makeup mirror from first meeting unfolds again; the half-rolled red carpet stops at the stage lip.
A-Tang carries the oil-stained face-pattern model book into the papier-mache atelier.
Those five tung-oil lamps under the atelier beam still burn; A-Tang checks them one by one along the posts.
On the windowsill, those earlier three cinnabar dishes still sit ranked by thickness.
A-Tang lifts the rebacked white-faced Cao Cao headdress and dips cinnabar to start the brush anew.
